In Greek mythology, this last king of Troy during the Trojan War was the father of Hector, Paris, and Cassandra — who was he?
Priam: Mythological king of Troy. In Greek mythology, Priam (Ancient Greek: Πρίαμος, pronounced [prí.amos]) was the legendary and last king of Troy during the Trojan War.

Beginning and ending with the sighting of a crescent moon, this 29-to-30-day observance is one of Islam's five pillars and the month when the Quran is believed to have been first revealed — what is it?
Ramadan: Ninth month of the Islamic calendar and month-long fasting event in Islam.
Ukraine's wealthiest man, this businessman owns FC Shakhtar Donetsk and has funneled hundreds of millions of dollars in wartime aid through his foundation — who is he?
Rinat Akhmetov: Ukrainian businessman. Rinat Leonidovych Akhmetov (born 21 September 1966) is a Ukrainian oligarch, billionaire and businessman.
Beginning in February 2014 with Russia's annexation of Crimea and a war in the Donbas, this conflict escalated into Europe's biggest war since World War II — what is it called?
Russo-Ukrainian war: Ongoing conflict since 2014. It then supported Russian separatist armed groups who started a war in the eastern Donbas region against Ukraine's military.
Leader of Spain's far-right Vox party since 2014 and president of Patriots.eu since 2024, this politician represents Madrid in the Congress of Deputies — who is he?
Lord of the desert and god of storms and chaos in ancient Egyptian religion, he murdered his own brother Osiris before being pursued for revenge by his nephew Horus — who is this god?
Set (deity): Egyptian god of the desert, storms, violence, and foreigners.
Nicknamed 'The White Death,' this Finnish marksman is credited with over 500 kills during the 1939-40 Winter War against the Soviets — who was he?

On 14 July 1789 in Paris, revolutionary insurgents fought for four hours and suffered 94 deaths to seize a medieval fortress-prison holding just seven inmates — which event kicked off a decade of upheaval in France?
Storming of the Bastille: Major event of the French Revolution.
This 18th-century French showman and soldier could swallow corks, stones, and live animals, and was constantly ravenous no matter how much he ate — who was he?
Tarrare: French showman and voracious eater (c. 1772–1798)
Called the "father of mindfulness," this Vietnamese Zen monk founded the Plum Village Tradition and was exiled in 1966 for opposing the war and refusing to take sides — who was he?
Thích Nhất Hạnh: Vietnamese Buddhist monk and activist (1926–2022)
This eighth Umayyad caliph ordered the first official collection of hadiths and sent emissaries as far as China and Tibet inviting rulers to accept Islam — who was he?
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: Umayyad caliph from 717 to 720.
Also called Narayana and Hari, this Hindu deity known as 'The Preserver' forms one third of the Trimurti alongside Brahma and Shiva — who is he?
This Luftwaffe ace was the first pilot in history to down 100 enemy aircraft and devised the famous finger-four formation — yet he died as a passenger in a plane crash. Who was he?
Werner Mölders: German World War II flying ace.
Elected tsar of Russia by the Seven Boyars in 1610 — though he never took that throne — this eldest son of Sigismund III went on to rule Poland and Lithuania; who is he?
Władysław IV Vasa: Ruler of Poland–Lithuania from 1632 to 1648.
This third-century queen of the Palmyrene Empire conquered Egypt and expanded her realm across the Roman East before facing Emperor Aurelian's counterattack — who is she?
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these was founded earliest?
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Joseph Henry is a physicist. Joseph Henry (December 17, 1797– May 13, 1878) was an American physicist and inventor who served as the first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
What is the atomic number of Roentgenium?
Roentgenium (German: [ʁœntˈɡeːni̯ʊm]) is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
What is the atomic number of Mercury?
Mercury is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
In what year was Claudine Gay born?
Claudine Gay (born August 4, 1970) is an American political scientist who is the Wilbur A.
In what year was Louis Pasteur born?
Louis Pasteur: Pasteur's works are credited with saving millions of lives through the developments of vaccines for rabies and anthrax.
In what year was Isaac Newton born?
Isaac Newton: Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
In what year did Alexander Fleming die?
Alexander Fleming: Sir Alexander Fleming (6 August 1881 – 11 March 1955) was a Scottish physician and microbiologist.
In what year did John Maynard Keynes die?
John Maynard Keynes: Keynes was educated at King's College at the University of Cambridge, where he graduated in 1904 with a B.A. in mathematics.
In what year was Iron discovered?
Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe (from Latin ferrum 'iron') and atomic number 26.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. Designed by the Soviet Union's Mikoyan-Gurevich bureau, it is an aircraft built primarily using stainless steel.
Which country is Aero L-39 Albatros from?
Aero L-39 Albatros: Czechoslovakia. The Aero L-39 Albatros is a high-performance jet trainer designed and produced by Aero Vodochody in the Czech Republic.
Who is credited with discovering Caelum?
Caelum: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Caelum SEE-ləm is a faint constellation in the southern sky, introduced in the 1750s by Nicolas Louis de Lacaille and counted among the 88 modern constellations.
Who is credited with discovering 243 Ida?
243 Ida: Johann Palisa. 243 Ida is an asteroid in the Koronis family of the asteroid belt.
Who is credited with discovering Gliese 581d?
Gliese 581d: Stéphane Udry. It was the third planet claimed in the system and the fourth (in a 4-planet model) or fifth (in a disproven 5- or 6-planet model) in order from the star.
Who is credited with discovering Chlorofluorocarbon?
Chlorofluorocarbon: Frédéric Swarts. The most common example of a CFC is dichlorodifluoromethane (R-12).

This Scottish physician's 1928 discovery of a mould-derived substance later named benzylpenicillin has been called the single greatest victory ever achieved over disease, and earned him a shared Nobel Prize in 1945 — who is he?
Alexander Fleming (6 August 1881 - 11 March 1955) was a Scottish physician and microbiologist.
This psychological term describes a diverse set of deficits in the ability to feel or anticipate pleasure, and is recognized as a diagnostic feature in the DSM-5 — what's the term?
Anhedonia is a diverse array of deficits in hedonic function, including reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure.
This general medical term describes a joint disorder in which the smooth cartilage lining wears away, leaving bone to grind directly on bone during movement — what condition is it?
Arthritis is a general medical term used to describe a disorder in which the smooth cartilagenous layer that lines a joint is lost, resulting in bone grinding on bone during joint movement.
Marketed early on as the Debonair in its conventional-tail form, this piston single has been built continuously longer than any other aircraft ever made — which model?
Beechcraft Bonanza is an American general aviation aircraft introduced in 1947 by Beech Aircraft Corporation of Wichita, Kansas.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
This flammable, colorless alkane gas with the formula C4H10 takes its name from a Greek word for butter, via butyric acid — what is it?
Butane is an alkane with the formula C4H10. Butane exists as two isomers, n-butane, CH3CH2CH2CH3 and iso-butane, (CH3)3CH.
Named for its habit of burrowing nests into dead wood or bamboo, this genus of some 500 bee species includes one soil-tunneling exception among its 31 subgenera — what insect is it?
Carpenter bee are species in the genus Xylocopa of the subfamily Xylocopinae.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks and rays — has a skeleton made almost entirely of cartilage, setting it apart from its bony-skeletoned relatives. What class is this?

Chondrichthyes (from Ancient Greek (khndros) 'cartilage' and (ikhths) 'fish') is a class of jawed fish that contains the cartilaginous fish or chondrichthyans, which all have skeletons primarily composed of cartilage.
Named for its snake-like neck (its species epithet means 'snake'), this feisty freshwater reptile has powerful beak-like jaws and ranges from Nova Scotia down to Florida — which species is it?
Common snapping turtle (Chelydra serpentina) is a species of large, freshwater turtles in the family Chelydridae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "dark blue," and its anion — a carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen — is so toxic that salts like the sodium and potassium forms cause swift poisoning. What is it?
Cyanide (from Greek kyanos 'dark blue') is an inorganic chemical compound that contains a CN functional group.
Known from thousands of fossils pulled from the La Brea Tar Pits, this extinct species of canine roamed the Americas until about 10,000 years ago. Name the species?
Dire wolf (Aenocyon dirus) is an extinct species of canine which was native to the Americas during the Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene epochs (125,000-10,000 years ago).
This mammal family includes living species from two genera as well as extinct giants like the woolly mammoth, and was first scientifically described in 1821 — what family is it?

Elephantidae is a family of large, herbivorous proboscidean mammals which includes the living elephants (belonging to the genera Elephas and Loxodonta), as well as a number of extinct genera like Mammuthus (mammoths) and Palaeoloxodon.

Built by a consortium of Airbus, BAE Systems and Leonardo for four NATO nations, this twin-engine canard delta-wing fighter grew out of the 1983 Future European Fighter Aircraft programme — which jet?
Eurofighter Typhoon is a European multinational twin-engine, supersonic, canard delta wing, multirole fighter.
This genus in the rose family includes more than 20 species prized for their sweet-to-tart edible fruits, with domestic hybrids grown worldwide — what is its scientific name?
Fragaria is a genus of flowering plants in the rose family, Rosaceae, commonly known as strawberries for their edible fruits.

Sometimes called the 'lesser apes' to distinguish them from chimpanzees, gorillas, and orangutans, these smaller, tailless primates live in forests from eastern Bangladesh through Southeast Asia and don't build nests — what are they?
Gibbon are apes in the family Hylobatidae (hylobatids).
This eel-shaped ocean scavenger defends itself by flooding predators with slime from glands in its skin — what creature is it?
Hagfish (also known as Hyperotreti) and order Myxiniformes, are eel-shaped jawless fish (occasionally called slime eels).
Also called the ratel, this animal is Africa's largest land-dwelling mustelid, armed with remarkably loose skin that lets it twist around and bite back even when grabbed. What is it?
Honey badger (Mellivora capensis), also known as the ratel (or), is a mammal widely distributed across Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.
This Russian-American aviation pioneer, a trailblazer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, won the top prize at the 1912 Moscow Aviation Exhibition for one of his early designs — who is he?
Igor Sikorsky (25 May 1889 - 26 October 1972) was a Russian-American aviation pioneer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.
Trained in biochemistry and physiology before ranging into geography and anthropology, this American author won the 1998 Pulitzer for Guns, Germs, and Steel — who is he?
Jared Diamond (born September 10, 1937) is an American scientist, historian, and author.
Born in 1972, this Canadian atmospheric scientist holds an endowed public-policy chair at Texas Tech and in 2021 became Chief Scientist at the Nature Conservancy — who is she?
Katharine Hayhoe (born 1972) is a Canadian atmospheric scientist.

A Cornell-trained engineer and Atlanta factory superintendent, this man was wrongly convicted of a young employee's murder, then kidnapped from prison and lynched in a case now central to American antisemitism — who was he?

Leo Frank (April 17, 1884 - August 17, 1915) was an American lynching victim wrongly convicted of the murder of 13-year-old Mary Phagan, an employee in a factory in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was the superintendent.
Credited as the 'Father of Cinematography' for filming Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888, this French inventor mysteriously vanished in 1890 before cinema took off — who was he?

Louis Le Prince (28 August 1841 - disappeared 16 September 1890; declared dead 16 September 1897) was a French artist and the inventor of an early motion-picture camera, and director of Roundhay Garden Scene.
This Italian economist served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022 after previously heading the European Central Bank for eight years and the Bank of Italy before that — who is he?

Mario Draghi (born 3 September 1947) is an Italian politician, economist, academic, banker, statesman, and civil servant, who served as the prime minister of Italy from 13 February 2021 to 22 October 2022.

Named from Greek words meaning 'small head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-normal head and can affect brain development, intellectual ability, and motor function — which disorder is it?
Microcephaly (from Neo-Latin microcephalia, from Ancient Greek mikrs "small" and kephal "head") is a medical condition involving a smaller-than-normal head.
This group of more than 30 rare neuromuscular disorders causes skeletal tissue to progressively weaken and break down, differing in which body parts are hit first and how fast — what's it called?
Muscular dystrophy (MD) is a genetically and clinically heterogeneous group of rare neuromuscular diseases that cause progressive weakness and breakdown of skeletal muscles over time.
Once confused with its chemical twin tantalum, this element with atomic number 41 resists corrosion so well it's used in earrings for people allergic to nickel — which element?
Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb (formerly columbium, Cb) and atomic number 41.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this fish-eating raptor nests near water and can be identified by its brown back and pale, grayish head — what bird is it?
Osprey (Pandion haliaetus), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.
Sometimes mistaken for wild pigs, these New World ungulates roam from the southwestern U.S. through Central and South America and into Trinidad — name the family?
Peccary (also javelinas or skunk pigs) are pig-like ungulates of the family Tayassuidae (New World pigs).

This subdiscipline of biology examines how organisms, organs, cells, and biomolecules carry out their chemical and physical functions, and its name derives from Greek words for 'nature' and 'study of' — what is it?
Physiology (from Ancient Greek (phsis) 'nature, origin' and - (-loga) 'study of') is the scientific study of functions and mechanisms in a living system.
A colorless salt that looks deceptively like sugar and dissolves easily in water, this compound is mostly used in gold mining — but a 200-to-300-milligram dose will kill nearly any human. What is it?
Potassium cyanide is a compound with the formula KCN.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes includes some of the world's largest and kills by coiling to suffocate rather than by injecting venom — what is the family called?

Pythonidae are a family of nonvenomous snakes found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
As chairman of the now-defunct Purdue Pharma, he oversaw the launch of OxyContin — a tenure dramatized in Hulu's Dopesick and Netflix's Painkiller; who is he?
Richard Sackler (born March 10, 1945) is an American businessman, pharmaceutical entrepreneur and physician who was the chairman and president of Purdue Pharma, a now-defunct pharmaceutical company.
Milder than most of its Allium relatives like garlic and leeks, this vegetable has a long, hollow green stem and no fully developed bulb — what is it commonly called?
Scallion (also known as green onions and spring onions) are edible vegetables of various species in the genus Allium.
With the formula AgNO3, this colorless, highly water-soluble compound is the least expensive salt of a lustrous precious metal and a precursor to many similar compounds — name it?
Silver nitrate is an inorganic compound with chemical formula AgNO3.
A self-taught Indian genius of infinite series and number theory, he initially struggled to interest established mathematicians because his methods were so unfamiliar — who was he?
Srinivasa Ramanujan (22 December 1887 - 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
A military engineer celebrated as a national hero in Poland, Lithuania, Belarus AND the United States, he fought for American independence before leading an 1794 uprising back home — who was he?

Tadeusz Kościuszko (4 or 12 February 1746 - 15 October 1817) was a Polish military engineer, statesman, and military leader who became a national hero in Poland, the United States, Lithuania, and Belarus.
What culinary herb — the dried aerial parts of plants in the mint family, native to the Mediterranean — is most commonly cultivated in its 'vulgaris' species from Southeast Europe?
Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria and contracted orally, this disease presents with gradual fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, rose-colored skin spots. What is it?
Typhoid fever is an orally contracted disease caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria, also called Salmonella Typhi.

This trailing vine of the gourd family bears a fruit that's botanically a 'pepo' — a hard-rinded berry with no internal divisions — and comes in more than 1,000 varieties, even seedless ones. What is it?
Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, that has a large, edible fruit.

This paraphilia describes a sexual fixation on non-human animals, distinct from acting on such attraction, and was estimated in one 2021 study to affect about 2 percent of the population — name the term?
Zoophilia is a paraphilia in which a person experiences a sexual fixation on non-human animals.
This practice leans on 'branding' — tying a name or image to certain qualities in people's minds — to nudge them toward buying more. What field is it?
Advertising: Form of communication for marketing.
This Swedish chemist held 355 patents, invented dynamite, and then left his fortune to fund a famous set of prizes. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel: Swedish chemist and inventor (1833–1896)
Ectothermic four-limbed vertebrates whose only living members are frogs, salamanders, and the worm-like caecilians — what class of animal is this?
Amphibian: Class of ectothermic tetrapods. The origin of modern lissamphibians, which first appeared during the Early Triassic, around 250 million years ago, has long been contentious.
Nicknamed 'Nastia' in the USSR and known to NATO as 'Curl,' this twin-engine turboprop military transport was later license-built in China under a different name — what aircraft is it?
Antonov An-26: Soviet turboprop transport aircraft. It is the third member of the Antonov An-24 family, coming after the An-24 and An-30, while preceding the An-32 and cancelled An-132.
Also called the yellow-legged predatory wasp, this insect — native to parts of Southeast Asia — has become an invasive concern across much of Europe — which species?
Asian hornet: Species of insect. The Asian hornet (Vespa velutina), also known as the yellow-legged hornet or Asian predatory wasp, is a species of hornet indigenous to Southeast Asia.
Instead of teeth, these marine mammals sieve plankton through whalebone plates in their mouths — a group of 16 species that includes the rorquals and the bowhead. What do we call them?
Known as silver birch for its peeling white bark, this deciduous tree native to Europe and Asia has become invasive in parts of North America — which species?
Betula pendula: Species of birch. Its range extends into Siberia, China, and southwest Asia in the mountains of northern Turkey, the Caucasus, and northern Iran.
Built to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a nose-mounted 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles, with a two-person tandem cockpit — which aircraft is it?

Boeing AH-64 Apache: U.S. attack helicopter. The Apache began as the Model 77 developed by Hughes Helicopters for the United States Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter program to replace the AH-1 Cobra.

Native to Europe, West Asia, and parts of North Africa, this widely introduced game fish is one of the world's worst invasive species outside its home range, with regional names like sewin in Wales and finnock in Scotland — which species is it?
Brown trout: Species of fish. Brown trout are highly adaptable and have evolved numerous ecotypes/subspecies.

Derived from an East Asian evergreen tree's wood, this waxy, strong-smelling terpenoid can also be synthesized from oil of turpentine and occurs in small amounts in rosemary leaves. What compound is it?
An obligate carnivore with retractable claws and crepuscular hunting habits, this small domesticated mammal communicates with everything from purrs and trills to hisses — what is it?
Cat: Small domesticated carnivorous mammal. The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal.
Nicknamed 'Vigorous Dragon' and known to NATO as the Firebird, this Chinese delta-wing, canard-design fighter jet has been exported to Pakistan's air force — which aircraft, capable of Mach 1.8?
Chengdu J-10: Chinese multi-role fighter aircraft family.
Named after the French missionary who propagated it in Algeria, this citrus hybrid of mandarin and sweet orange is often sold as an 'Easy-peeler' — which fruit?
Clementine: Hybrid citrus fruit. The exterior is a deep orange colour with a smooth, glossy appearance.

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
Nicknamed the mosquito hawk, which long-legged insect of the superfamily Tipuloidea is often mistaken for an oversized mosquito?
Crane fly: Superfamily of flies. The larvae of crane flies are known commonly as leatherjackets.
First created in 1994 and named for the German city where it was made, this synthetic element sits below platinum in group 10 — what is it?
Darmstadtium: Chemical element with atomic number 110 (Ds)
Produced by the enzyme 5α-reductase acting on a more familiar male sex hormone, this compound is a more potent driver of prostate growth, sebum, and body hair — which hormone?
Sometimes called 'word blindness,' this learning disability makes it hard to spell, sound out words, and read quickly, and often co-occurs with ADHD — what is it?
The tallest and heaviest of all living penguins, this flightless Antarctic bird can top 45 kilograms and sports bright-yellow ear patches — which species is it?
Emperor penguin: Large flightless seabird endemic to Antarctica.
This Marine-turned-professor's 1981 memoir about fighting at Peleliu and Okinawa later inspired Ken Burns's The War and HBO's The Pacific, where he was played by Joseph Mazzello — who is he?
Found on birds and even some non-avian dinosaurs, this complex evolutionary structure aids flight, insulation and waterproofing, and gives its name to the study of plumology — what is it?

Members of this insect order have just one pair of true wings — the hindwings evolved into balance organs called halteres — and the group includes mosquitoes among its 150,000+ species. What are they commonly called?
Fly: Order of insects. A fly (pl. flies) is an insect of the order Diptera (from Ancient Greek δι- di- 'two' and πτερόν pteron 'wing'), named for the single pair of wings.
Capable of living up to 177 years and weighing as much as 417 kilograms, which giant reptile — native to a chain of Pacific islands named for it — is the largest cold-blooded land animal alive today?
Galápagos tortoise: Species of reptile. The species comprises 15 subspecies (12 extant and 3 extinct).
Found in birds, crocodilians, and earthworms alike, this thick-muscled digestive organ grinds food with the help of swallowed grit — what's it called?
Gizzard: Digestive organ of some animals.

Once classified as a subfamily of the seabasses, this diverse family of marine ray-finned fish is now treated as distinct, with most members drawn from two large genera. What are they commonly called?
Grouper: Family of fishes. The common name "grouper" is usually given to fish in one of two large genera: Epinephelus and Mycteroperca.
Nicknamed bindwood or lovestone, this clinging evergreen native to Europe scales tree trunks, walls, and fences — which plant?
Hedera helix: Species of flowering plant.
This genus of over 570 flowering plants — the only living genus in its family — includes the evergreen shrub famous for Christmas decorations and cards. What genus is it?
Holly: Genus of flowering plants. Ilex or holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.
This immune response causes tissue damage upon repeated exposure to an antigen and underlies conditions like hay fever, which affects roughly one in ten people worldwide — what is it called?
Hypersensitivity: Overreaction of the immune system to an antigen.
This sugar alcohol, with about half the sweetness of table sugar, is made by the human kidney at roughly two grams a day and reaches its highest concentration in the brain — what is it?
Inositol: Carbocyclic sugar. Its formula is C6H12O6; the molecule has a ring of six carbon atoms, each with a hydrogen atom and a hydroxy group (–OH).
Often mislabeled 'yellowtail tuna' on sushi menus, this northwest Pacific jack fish is unrelated to true tuna and is called hamachi when served as sashimi — which species?
Japanese amberjack: Species of fish. The Japanese amberjack or yellowtail, Seriola quinqueradiata, is a species of jack fish in the family Carangidae, native to the northwest Pacific Ocean.
Also known as the English or Persian walnut, this tree species native to Eurasia is cultivated worldwide, with China as its leading producer today — what is it?
Juglans regia: Species of tree (walnut). Juglans regia, known by various common names including the common walnut, English walnut, or Persian walnut amongst other names, is a species of walnut.
Named from a Norwegian word for 'small fry of fish,' these shrimp-like crustaceans form a biomass of some 379 million tonnes in the Southern Ocean alone — which creatures?

Krill: Small, shrimp-like crustaceans; order of crustaceans. Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.
Also called Hansen's disease, this slow bacterial infection dulls the body's sense of pain so badly that unnoticed injuries can cost a person their fingers and toes — what is it?
Leprosy: Chronic disease caused by bacterial infection.
Born as a Skunk Works black project and nicknamed "Habu," this Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft carried a crew of two in tandem cockpits — which plane is it?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: US Air Force supersonic aircraft, 1964–1998.
First named in 1703 to honor a French botanist, this genus of 200-plus flowering trees and shrubs produces large fragrant blooms and cone-like autumn fruits — which genus?
Magnolia: Genus of angiosperms. Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
Born in Erfurt in 1864, this German jurist-turned-scholar became one of the founding figures of sociology before a breakdown following his father's death halted his teaching — who was he?
Max Weber: German sociologist, jurist, and political economist (1864–1920)
This field studies how we study — analyzing, comparing, and evaluating the procedures researchers use to gather and interpret data, shaped by underlying philosophical assumptions. What is it called?
Following the S phase and ending in cytokinesis, this equational cell division splits replicated chromosomes into two genetically identical daughter nuclei — what is the process called?
Mitosis: Cell division into two identical cells. Mitosis is a part of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
Described by Eric Kandel as the 'epic challenge' of biology, this multidisciplinary field studies the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system — what field is it?
Neuroscience: Scientific study of the nervous system.

Producing a distinctive capped nut and supporting more than 950 species of caterpillar, this keystone hardwood genus ranges across the Northern Hemisphere in some 500 species, some evergreen, some deciduous — what tree is it?
Oak: Tree or shrub in the genus Quercus.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?
A Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner, he coined the word 'conurbation' and gave us one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally' in social science — who was he?
Patrick Geddes: Scottish scientist and town planner (1854–1932)
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Nicknamed the 'Bone,' this variable-sweep-wing heavy bomber was dreamed up to fuse the B-58's Mach 2 speed with the B-52's range and payload — which aircraft is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer: American strategic bomber.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?
Rising from general secretary in 1981 to FIFA's eighth president in 1998, this Swiss administrator won re-election four times before being suspended in the 2015 corruption scandal — who is he?
